items.title: Artie Shaw — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: [Mischa] Elman. People said, “You must have been a great teacher.” He said, “No, I had damn good pupils. I had very good pupils. As a matter of fact, I had one pupil you never heard of. He could play better than Heifetz or any of them.” “No kidding? Why haven’t we ever heard of him?” He said, “Well he can’t play for anybody.” That’s a marvelous joke. Very subtle. If you can’t do it, there’s no use. I can write fine, but when I sit down to write, I freeze. I can do it in here. The other line of course is the old…

I had some very interesting things happen with the band. I never told many people this one. You know how I kept Billy Butterfield in the band? Billy was a very fine player, but he got very restless. Like Dodo. He would just quit and go somewhere else.
